paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where “Base” denotes LLM without editing.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the average co-occurrence (ACC) percentage across various co-occurrence numbers for different editing methods applied to a language model. The x-axis represents co-occurrence number, ranging from 1e1 to 1e10, with a linear scale and tick intervals of 10, starting at 1e1 and ending at 1e10. The y-axis represents the ACC percentage, measured in percent, ranging from approximately 40% to 65%, with a linear scale and tick intervals of 5, beginning at 40% and ending at 65%. A black solid line, denoted as “Base”, displays a steady decline from approximately 42% to 40% across the x-axis. A brown dashed line, labeled “MEND”, increases from approximately 45% to 55% across the x-axis. A teal solid line, labeled “FT”, increases from approximately 48% to 58% across the x-axis. A red solid line, labeled “IKE”, increases from approximately 40% to 45% across the x-axis. A purple solid line, labeled “MEMIT”, increases from approximately 43% to 53% across the x-axis. And a green solid line, labeled “ROME”, increases from approximately 43% to 55% across the x-axis.
